headline: Commodore launches flip phone that blocks social media and browsers
summary: The Callback 8020 runs Sailfish OS, offering a de-Googled experience with system-level blocks on social media apps and web browsers, starting at $499.
details: The resurrected Commodore brand is back with the Callback 8020, a flip phone designed as a nostalgic retreat from modern smartphone distractions. It features patent-pending technology to block social media apps, web browsers, and email clients at the system level, aiming to foster "real communication."

Running on the Linux-based Sailfish OS, the Callback 8020 offers a de-Googled experience and compatibility with over 99% of Android apps via a Runtime compatibility layer. This includes popular services like WhatsApp, Maps, and Spotify, while deliberately excluding "doomscrolling" applications.

Commodore emphasizes user privacy, promising not to collect or monetize data without consent, and to avoid tracking cookies. Despite the browser ban, the phone maintains an internet connection for essential functions like QR code scanning and navigation.

The device boasts a 3.25-inch main display and a 1.77-inch front display, powered by a MediaTek Helio G81 processor with 4GB of RAM and 64GB of storage, expandable via microSD. It features a 48MP rear camera, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and GPS.

Nostalgic touches include pre-loaded Commodore 64 games, an exterior display inspired by 1970s calculators, an 8-bit SID music player with SID ringtones, and a built-in DAC with included HD in-ear monitors.

The Commodore Callback 8020 is set to be available later in 2026, with pricing starting at $499 for the Basic Beige, ProtoPET White, and SX Silver colorways. More premium editions, including a 24k gold plated Founders Edition, will also be offered.
